newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Appointment of Dhaka bourse chief mainly welcomed.
newsitem.headline: Appointment of Dhaka bourse chief mainly welcomed.

text.p: Bangladesh's capital market on Monday mainly welcomed the appointment of a new chairman of the Dhaka Stock Exchange (DSE), and analysts said the move was expected to boost market sentiment.
The DSE governing council, acting in connection with alleged share price manipulation, on Sunday removed Imtiyaz Husain and named Abdul Huq Howlader the new chairman of the stock exchange.
Broker Abdur Rashid said investors wanted a change after the share market scandal. He praised the new chairman as "straight forward and energetic".
"I believe things should now turn better. The appointment of a new DSE chairman will infuse dynamism into the market," he said.
"Share prices have started rising. The prices came down so low recently that it should now move up", he added.
The stock market has been dogged by allegations of widespread share price manipulation since stock prices started falling sharply after a four-month rally.

Last month, an inquiry committee appointed by the Securities and Exchange Commission said 36 top dealers and owners of listed companies had been involved in "fraudulent activities" that created excess price volatility and led to huge loses for investors.
The accused included Husain, who has described the inquiry report as "baseless and motivated".

The DSE benchmark index shot up from below 1,000 to more than 3,600 in the first week of October, helped by euphoric trading in the unofficial kerb market not long after the election of Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina in June 1996.
The index stood at 1,083.79 at the close of trading on Sunday. Friday is the weekend in Moslem Bangladesh.
Broker Mostaque Ahmed said company fundamentals looked strong enough to push the index back up to the 1,550 level in the near future.
"Company fundamentals are basically sound. Some of the companies made tremendous profit last year," he said.
Meanwhile, the sacked chief said he would seek legal protection against his dismissal.
"I have not resigned and they (councillors) held an illegal no-confidence election without any agenda and proper notice," Husain told Reuters on Monday.
He said the action of the council, whose two-year term ends December, was unconstitutional and without precedence.
"Under the DSE constitution, it can only be done by an extraordinary AGM (annual general meeting) where a three-fourth majority is required to make any change of any kind," he said.
"I will seek justice in the court of law," he added.
But the new chairman said he had been appointed under the DSE constitution and there had been no violation of rules.
"The investors may come forward with fresh commitments when they see new faces in the bourse management," said former DSE chairman and broker Khurshid Alam.
Broker Mohammad Ullah said: "Investors' confidence will return due to the change in the administration. A positive sentiment in the market may push the share prices up."
But broker Syed Tareque Mohammad Ali expressed concerns about the way Husain had been removed.
"You must give him (Husain) a chance to defend himself. It's not fair when there is a case against him in the court and the charges made have not yet been proved," he said.
"It's difficult to say whether the market will improve by the change", he added. "Some people say it will, but I am not sure about it."
